name: @qontinui/cloud-control
description: Cloud extension to qontinui-web — powers the qontinui.cloud deployment (billing, multi-tenant routing, cloud-admin). AGPL-3.0; not published to npm (consumed as a file: path dependency).
//: No `test` script on purpose: the previous `vitest run` could not run (vitest was not a dependency, and neither a config nor a test file existed). A JS suite here needs the host app's `@/*` alias graph, since this package compiles inside qontinui-web. See .qontinui/ci.toml. The scripts/ gates are tested by `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts`.
//exports: No `exports` map on purpose. `main` alone is what qontinui-web's dynamic `import("@qontinui/cloud-control")` resolves, and adding `exports` would ALSO make it an encapsulation boundary that hides every subpath not listed. Wildcard targets do no extension resolution either, so a single `./services/*` pattern cannot serve both .ts and .tsx. This claim is now GATED rather than asserted: `scripts/check_frontend_imports.py` fails the build if any file under frontend/src imports this package by its own name, so a deep-import consumer cannot appear unnoticed. Intra-package imports must be relative; host imports use the `@/` alias.
//peerDependencies: NO `@qontinui/web` ENTRY, and its absence is the fix for a real defect. No package by that name exists in the workspace — qontinui-web/frontend/package.json declares `"name": "frontend"` (and is `private`), and neither its tsconfig `paths` nor its next.config `resolve.alias` maps the specifier. The peer dep was therefore unsatisfiable, and `frontend/src/index.ts` imported `@qontinui/web/lib/extension-slots` through it, so this package's ONLY entry point failed to resolve — silently, because layout.tsx loads it with `.catch(() => {})`. The host relationship is expressed by the `@/*` tsconfig alias of the app this package compiles inside, not by a package dependency.
